newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares erase gains to finish lower.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares erase gains to finish lower.

text.p: Bombay shares erased initial gains to finish lower on Thursday with select blue-chips hogging market spotlight, traders said.
"There is no major factor playing in the market -- Some expectations about fresh buying didn't materialise," said Dheeraj Agarwal, dealer at SSKI Securities.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index lost 30.52 points or 0.95 percent to a provisional 3,196.28, a touch above its intra-day low of 3,190.36.
Dealers said a fall in the SBI price amidst heavy volumes after a firm start, dragged blue-chips lower.
SBI lost 10.75 rupees to 239.0, after hitting the day's peak of 252.75 in volumes of 8.5 million shares. It lost 6.0 to 240.25 at the National bourse with 2.82 billion shares traded.
Pivotals including Reliance, TISCO and L&T finished lower.
"Market focus is on SBI. The pricing of its GDR issue is being keenly awaited," said a dealer.
Traders said few foreign funds were sellers in SBI. India's largest commerical bank is expected to price its $400 million GDR issue in the U.S. later on Thursday.
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) 50-stock index ended 10.95 points, or 1.17 percent lower at a provisional 925.05.

Telecom stock MTNL and tobacco major ITC figured among winning stocks. Fund buying pushed up MTNL 7.50 rupees to 213.0 while heavy speculative buying by Calcutta-based operators helped ITC gain 10.50 to 312.75, traders said.
ACC lost 69.50 to 1,690.50, Reliance 1.75 to 189, TISCO 0.25 to 171, L&T 2.25 to 229.25 and TELCO 10.50 to 433.25.
Dealers said lack of major market-moving news will keep the market in a narrow range, focus to stay on select blue-chips.
"The outlook for the market continues to remain dull and weak," SSKI's Agarwal said.
